rows: Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '3', address %B0C9
Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '2', address %B0C2
Simulate 85% to produce a trip on high bearing metal temperature for bearing '2', address %B0C2
Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '4', address %B0D3
Simulate 85% to produce a trip on high bearing metal temperature for bearing '4', address %B0D3
Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '6', address %B0C4
Simulate 85% to produce a trip on high bearing metal temperature for bearing '4', address %B0C4
Cancel the simulation on one of the two turbine inlet steam pressure signals, %B0DC and %B0D0, to trip the turbine on differential pressure protection across the turbine front, right and left.

Carry out the Turbomax test, i.e. thermal stresses on the turbine shaft, by making a 20% difference between the two signals %B0D2 and %D0C3, and the following signals appear: TT52 MEASUREMENT, LIMITER 52, TURBINE TRIP
Carry out the trip test on loss of vacuum by cancelling the simulation on the two vacuum measurement transmitters, addresses %B0D5 and %B0D9; the turbine trips instantaneously.
Carry out the trip test on loss of vacuum after 10 minutes, by cancelling the simulation on one of the vacuum measurement transmitters, addresses %B0D5 or %B0D9
Carry out the Vibration test; to carry out this test the turbine shaft speed must be greater than 2%, i.e. greater than 37 rpm, and the Vibration sensors are located on turbine bearings 1, 3 and 4
Simulate '1' on bearing '1' to produce a high 1 signal, address B031
Simulate '1' on bearing '1' to produce a high 2 signal, address B032
Simulate '1' on bearing '3' to produce a high 1 signal, address B430
Simulate '1' on bearing '3' to produce a high 2 signal, address B530
Simulate '1' on bearing '4' to produce a high 1 signal, address B630
Simulate '1' on bearing '4' to produce a high 2 signal, address B730
For the turbine to trip on Vibration protection, a high 1 signal must appear from any bearing and a high 2 signal from any other bearing at the same time (done by connecting the computer to CH1)
Carry out the turbine trip test on the bearing lubricating oil pressure dropping to 0.6 x PL
This is done by actually leaking oil by opening the oil leak valve inside the turbine body
Carry out the turbine trip test on the bearing lubricating oil pressure dropping to 0.4 x PL, with the DC emergency pump starting
Carry out the emergency trip test of the turbine from the thermal control room
Carry out the emergency trip test of the turbine by means of the red handwheel on the turbine body
Carry out the turbine trip test when the turbine speed reaches zero
Carry out the turbine trip test via GENERATOR PROTECTION

Introduction
This document sets out the tests carried out on the unit; the purpose of these tests is to test the operation of the protection devices on the turbine. They are carried out after the completion of periodic maintenance work and before the unit is connected to the grid, to make sure the unit's protection devices operate correctly, so that they operate in the event of any fault in the unit during operation.
The document was prepared by Eng. Ayman Mohamed Abdel Meguid, reviewed and tested by Eng. Mohamed Abdel Mohsen, endorsed by Eng. Abdel Azim Gomaa Hagras, General Manager, approved by Mr. Eng. Hussein Ahmed El-Mahdy, Head of the Assiut Steam Power Station Sector, and certified by Eng. Gamal El-Din Abdel Wahab, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector and MPIS Coordinator at the Upper Egypt Electricity Production Company.
Safety precautions

Procedures to be carried out
Preliminary steps
Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '3', address %B0C9
Tests on CH1:
Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '2', address %B0C2 | 1.
Simulate 85% to produce a trip on high bearing metal temperature for bearing '2', address %B0C2 | 2.
Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '4', address %B0D3 | 3.
Simulate 85% to produce a trip on high bearing metal temperature for bearing '4', address %B0D3 | 4.
Simulate 65% to produce a bearing metal temperature alarm for bearing '6', address %B0C4 | 5.
Simulate 85% to produce a trip on high bearing metal temperature for bearing '4', address %B0C4 | 6.
Cancel the simulation on one of the two turbine inlet steam pressure signals, %B0DC and %B0D0, to trip the turbine on differential pressure protection across the turbine front, right and left. | 7.
Carry out the Turbomax test, i.e. thermal stresses on the turbine shaft, by making a 20% difference between the two signals %B0D2 and %D0C3, and the following signals appear: TT52 MEASUREMENT, LIMITER 52, TURBINE TRIP | 8.
Carry out the trip test on loss of vacuum by cancelling the simulation on the two vacuum measurement transmitters, addresses %B0D5 and %B0D9; the turbine trips instantaneously. | 9.
Carry out the trip test on loss of vacuum after 10 minutes, by cancelling the simulation on one of the vacuum measurement transmitters, addresses %B0D5 or %B0D9 | 10.
Carry out the Vibration test; to carry out this test the turbine shaft speed must be greater than 2%, i.e. greater than 37 rpm, and the Vibration sensors are located on turbine bearings 1, 3 and 4
Simulate '1' on bearing '1' to produce a high 1 signal, address B031 | 1.
Simulate '1' on bearing '1' to produce a high 2 signal, address B032 | 2.
Simulate '1' on bearing '3' to produce a high 1 signal, address B430 | 3.
Simulate '1' on bearing '3' to produce a high 2 signal, address B530 | 4.
Simulate '1' on bearing '4' to produce a high 1 signal, address B630 | 5.
Simulate '1' on bearing '4' to produce a high 2 signal, address B730 | 6.
For the turbine to trip on Vibration protection, a high 1 signal must appear from any bearing and a high 2 signal from any other bearing at the same time (done by connecting the computer to CH1) | 
Part Two: Practical tests
Carry out the turbine trip test on the bearing lubricating oil pressure dropping to 0.6 x PL | 1.
This is done by actually leaking oil by opening the oil leak valve inside the turbine body | 
Carry out the turbine trip test on the bearing lubricating oil pressure dropping to 0.4 x PL, with the DC emergency pump starting | 2.
Carry out the emergency trip test of the turbine from the thermal control room | 3.
Carry out the emergency trip test of the turbine by means of the red handwheel on the turbine body | 4.
Carry out the turbine trip test when the turbine speed reaches zero | 5.
Carry out the turbine trip test via GENERATOR PROTECTION | 6.

uncertain_terms.note: Inconsistent in the source: step 5 assigns address %B0C4 to bearing '6', step 6 assigns the same address %B0C4 to bearing '4'; preserved verbatim.
Source 'LIMETER52' is garbled; rendered 'LIMITER 52' (with TT52 MEASUREMENT and TURBINE TRIP).
Signal addresses in the Turbomax step are garbled in the source ('D0C3% B0D2%'); rendered as %B0D2 and %D0C3.
Steam pressure signal addresses in step 7 are garbled in the source; rendered as %B0DC and %B0D0.
Source notation 'x0.6PL' rendered as '0.6 x PL' (pressure limit factor); the unit/symbol is unexplained in the source.
Rendered 'red handwheel' (manual trip handle on the turbine body); the source says 'the red hand'.
Source states shaft speed greater than 2%, i.e. greater than 37 rpm; preserved verbatim (implies a rated speed of about 1850 rpm, not stated).
